cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Make the Choice Rewrite the Past
cards.instruction: Make them choose between options whose consequences reinterpret an earlier promise, refusal, or agreement.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep my key or give it back. Let's settle what you meant by needing space last week.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I wanted one quiet evening, not a breakup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep it, then. I'll call that evening finished and put your name back on the buzzer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Keeping a key doesn't mean you can turn up at mine whenever you like.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll phone first. Keep it for visiting, or hand it back if that evening really was goodbye.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 forces key choice to reinterpret space; A5 offers phoning first, but A3 buzzer action does not cause B4 concern about visiting B own home.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 denies breakup and A3 restores buzzer name; B4 switches homes without a stated reciprocal visit proposal.

relationship.evidence: B4 access boundary is plausible in itself but not specifically prompted by A3 action.

heightening.evidence: A5 phoning addresses B4 yet repairs a new concern the prior turn did not prepare.

specificity.evidence: A3 name back on buzzer implies prior removal and perhaps residence, neither necessary nor explained.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 added buzzer history distracts from the key and earlier quiet evening.
